title: A return by hand
blurb: From slips to total income, taxable income, tax and a refund.

levels.title: From slips to taxable income
learn: Add up Priya's slips to get total income.
Take off her deductions to reach net income and taxable income.

cards.text: In this unit you work out Priya's whole tax return by hand, one step at a time, from the slips you have already read. The steps run in order: total income, deductions, taxable income, tax, and then a refund or a balance owing.

image.alt: A desk with a blank form and a row of blank slips

cards.text: This return is for the 2025 tax year, the same year the tax program your class uses files in December.

image.alt: A desk lamp over an empty open notebook and a grey folder

cards.text: Step 1 is total income, line 15000: all the income on your slips, added up. Priya's income slips are her T4 and her T5. Her T5 interest goes into total income too. Her RRSP receipt is not income, so it stays out of this step.

Deductions come off total income. Priya's first is her RRSP contribution of $1,200, on line 20800. A deduction is an amount you may subtract before tax is worked out. Apart from the two on these cards, she has no deductions in this unit.

image.alt: A wooden savings box beside a pencil

cards.text: Her second deduction is line 22215. In plain words, it is a deduction for part of the CPP you paid. Box 16 of her T4 shows $1,428 of CPP. $1,188 of it earns a credit, which you use in level 2. The rest is the deduction.

image.alt: A jar and two stacks of gold discs on a shelf

cards.text: Total income minus the deductions is net income, line 23600. Priya has no other deductions, so her taxable income, line 26000, is the same amount. Tax is worked out on taxable income.

levels.title: Federal tax
learn: Work out federal tax on taxable income from the first band.
Work out each credit and net federal tax.

cards.text: Tax is worked out on taxable income, which for Priya is $26,123.50. The federal tax table has bands. A band is a slice of income taxed at one rate. Her first band taxes income up to $57,375 at 14.5%, and all her taxable income fits in it.

image.alt: A ruler across a row of wooden blocks on a desk

cards.text: So her federal tax on taxable income is taxable income x 14.5%. Round the answer to the nearest cent. This is the tax before credits. Next come the credits, which lower it.

image.alt: A brass calculator with a blank screen beside gold discs

cards.text: A non-refundable tax credit lowers the tax you owe, but cannot take it below $0. Each credit here is an amount x the lowest federal rate, 14.5%. Round each credit to the nearest cent.

image.alt: A stack of gold discs with a few lifted onto a blank tag

cards.text: Priya's four credit amounts. The base CPP amount is the part of box 16 that earns a credit. The EI amount is box 18. Her pay is above the Canada employment amount, so she gets all of it.

Add the four credits. Then take the total away from the federal tax on taxable income. What is left is net federal tax, line 42000. If the credits were bigger than the tax, the answer would stop at $0.

levels.title: Alberta tax and the bottom line
learn: Work out Alberta tax, total tax and the refund.
Say what the RRSP deduction did to her return.

cards.text: Alberta has its own tax, worked out on the same taxable income. Priya's first Alberta band taxes income up to $60,000 at 8%, and all of her taxable income fits in it. Alberta tax on taxable income is taxable income x 8%, to the nearest cent.

image.alt: A small wooden prairie map with a flag, a ruler and a pencil

cards.text: Alberta credits work like the federal ones, but each is an amount x the lowest Alberta rate, 8%. Priya has three. Round each credit to the nearest cent, add them, and take the total off the Alberta tax.

Total tax is net federal tax plus Alberta tax after credits. The tax withheld is T4 box 22, which goes on line 43700. A refund, line 48400, is the tax withheld minus the total tax, when that is above $0.

image.alt: A balance scale with gold discs against a blank slip

cards.text: If the total tax is more than the tax withheld, the difference is a balance owing instead, line 48500. A refund and a balance owing are two answers to the same subtraction, one on each side of $0.

image.alt: A tilted balance scale with a blank slip on the low side

cards.text: Here is the whole chain for Priya, from her slips to her refund. Each row comes from the row or rows above it.

What did the RRSP do? Work the return again with no RRSP deduction. Her taxable income is $1,200 higher. In her first band each extra dollar is taxed at 14.5% federal plus 8% Alberta. Her credits and the tax withheld do not change.

options.why: That is her refund with the RRSP deduction. Without it her tax is higher.
Her tax would be more than what was withheld, so she would owe, not get a refund.
That is how much the RRSP lowered her tax, not what she would owe.
